goal: Produce an executable, deduplicated live-test matrix for sketch.trim (step 2 of preTrim->trim->postTrim). trim is well-characterized from the completed preTrim session (returns VOID/maxLevel31; atomic-fail mL51/1006 on bogus id; silent mL31 no-op on a source/original id = footgun #155; multiple trim() before one postTrim OK; nothing-staged = mL31 no-op; consumes only preTrim.result splittedCurves[].id). This matrix spends its budget ONLY on trim-SPECIFIC gaps the preTrim session did not cover: (1) the SCALE/HANG question — does trim inherit the trimCurves 39-segment kill-9 hang (TODO, build-lever-bracket session) — via a BOUNDED, risk-flagged graduated probe capped at <=30 segments on a lightly-constrained grid; (2) BULK semantics — trim multiple/all segments of a source, trim every segment, order-independence, untrimmed-id stability; (3) ARC segments from a cut circle vs line segments; (4) STATE — where a trimmed seg id goes (immediate death vs deferred; container childCount deltas); (5) VALIDATION edges trim adds beyond preTrim — empty [], missing curveIds, duplicate [s,s], stale/dead seg id, cross-sketch seg id, mixed valid+bad atomicity, curveIds type-list; (6) round-trip completion and minimal solver-independence. Each script tests ONE focused thing with a concrete numeric measurement. All proven facts cited to preTrim.md, NOT re-scripted.
questions: Does trim inherit the trimCurves many-segment hang? If so, at what segment count / constraint density does the trim call slow super-linearly or peg the worker (bounded probe <=30 segs, lightly constrained, never 39)?
What is the trim-call wall-clock duration trend (trimMs) vs staged segment count N across rungs ~12/~24/<=30 on a lightly-constrained grid?

When trim removes a staged segment, does that segment id die IMMEDIATELY (getPositions mL51 before postTrim) or persist until postTrim? Does SplittedCurves childCount drop, or does the trimmed id move to NoneSplitted?
Can you trim 3/5/many segments in one call atomically? Is curveIds order-independent (e.g. [A,B] vs [B,A] yield identical geometry)?
Does trimming segment A churn the id of an untrimmed sibling segment B (before postTrim)?
If you trim ALL segments of one source curve, does that source vanish entirely after postTrim, and do crossing cutter curves survive intact?
If you trim EVERY staged segment then postTrim, do you get an empty sketch (geometry arrays length 0) or an error? Do leftover points / leaked NoneSplitted0 containers remain?
Does trim accept a CIRCLE arc segment (from a doubly-cut circle) the same as a line segment (VOID/mL31), and does the survivor arc get a new id with correct endpoints?
Is curveIds:[] a safe mL31 no-op (NOT a 'trim all' footgun, unlike preTrim's []=all)? What happens on missing curveIds entirely (1004 vs no-op)?
Is a duplicate seg id [s,s] in one call idempotent (trimmed once, mL31) or a double-free error?
Is a STALE/dead segment id (from an earlier preTrim killed by re-preTrim, or post-commit) rejected as non-existent (1006) or silently ignored as not-currently-staged (mL31 no-op)?

Is a seg id from ANOTHER sketch rejected by global existence (passes type check, 1006 for not-in-this-sketch) or wrong-type (1001), i.e. does trim scope curveIds to this sketch's staging like splitCurve does NOT (footgun #154)?

In a mixed batch valid+bogus, does the call atomic-fail (mL51/1006) leaving the valid seg measurably untouched (getPositions returns original endpoints)? Does valid+sourceId (silent no-op element) poison the call or trim the valid seg while ignoring the source?
Does re-trimming an already-trimmed (but not yet committed) seg id mL31 no-op or 1006?
Does trim work on a planeless (solver-dead) sketch for both a line seg and an arc seg, confirming inherited solver-independence?
What is trim's curveIds type-list in the 1001 message (['sketch-curve'] like preTrim, or narrower)?
setupNotes: DESIGN-ONLY output; the main agent executes serially on the single shared worker. Harness pattern (proven, reuse verbatim): each script is `export default async function(api,{filewrite})`; import helpers from the preTrim session's _setup.mjs at /Users/dev/dev/awv/classcad-agent/workspace/training/2026-06-30_12-44-12_sketch-preTrim/scripts/_setup.mjs (makeSketch, addSketch, addPlanelessSketch, line, circle, positions->{maxLevel,startPos,endPos,pos}, containers(tree)->[{id,name,childCount,parent}] found by NAME, nodeById, centerPos for whole-circle parts, vecApprox, firstError). CRITICAL: part.create works ONLY ONCE per harness run (2nd call returns VOID and poisons the drawing) — call makeSketch ONCE per script, build all extra sketches via addSketch/addPlanelessSketch. New scripts live under /Users/dev/dev/awv/classcad-agent/workspace/training/2026-06-30_13-59-28_sketch-trim/scripts/. Measurement conventions: capture maxLevel LITERALLY on every call (never assume 31); VOID = result===null; collect staged seg ids as preResult.result.flatMap(e => e.splittedCurves.map(s => s.id)) and filewrite the COUNT before any trim (so a hang loses no setup data); inspect staging via containers(tree) by NAME (SplittedCurves/NoneSplitted/leaked NoneSplitted0), report childCount deltas; spatial claims need vecApprox numeric proof per SOUL.md (getPositions endpoints, not snapshots); circle/whole-circle parts reject getPositions -> use centerPos. Canonical cheap fixture: cross of one horizontal line h=[0,50]->[100,50] and one vertical v=[50,0]->[50,100] crossing at (50,50) -> preTrim yields 4 segments (2 per source). PROVEN facts (CITE preTrim.md, do NOT re-script): trim VOID/mL31; atomic-fail mL51/1006 on bogus id valid-untouched; silent mL31 no-op on source/original id (#155); multiple trim() before one postTrim; nothing-staged mL31 no-op; trim consumes only splittedCurves[].id, getGeometry mid-workflow shows originals; trim([]) and no-trim postTrim cleanly restore originals; contiguous survivors of a trimmed curve coalesce, survivors get NEW ids, untrimmed keep originals, Auto_Coinc recreated at cut vertex; preTrim error map id-missing 1004 / non-existent 1006 (+ preceding L41 ToId warn) / wrong-type id 1001 ['sketch'] / wrong-type curveIds elem 1001 ['sketch-curve']; preTrim/trim solver-independent on planeless sketch. Related footgun #154: splitCurve resolves geomId GLOBALLY (not scoped to the id sketch) — script 07 probes whether trim's curveIds inherits this cross-sketch leniency. HANG SAFETY: only script 03 approaches scale; it is bounded <=30 segs, lightly-constrained (planeId present but ZERO manual dimensions, auto-constraints only), each trim call timing-guarded, run LAST, main agent ready to kill -9. All other scripts use <=4-12 segments and <=2-id trims so they cannot hang.

scripts.title: trim staging mutation: where does a trimmed seg id go, immediately?
scripts.question: When trim removes a staged segment, does its id die immediately (getPositions mL51 before postTrim) or persist until postTrim? Does SplittedCurves childCount drop or does the id move to NoneSplitted?
scripts.setup: makeSketch (planeId). Build canonical cross h=[0,50]->[100,50], v=[50,0]->[50,100]. preTrim({id}) -> h,v each split at (50,50) into 2 segs (4 total). Capture staging baseline via containers(tree) from preResult.structure.tree (or getGeometry({id}).structure.tree): record SplittedCurves.childCount and NoneSplitted.childCount. Identify the left-half h overhang seg leftH = [0,50]->[50,50] by positions() endpoint match.
scripts.call: positions(leftH) BEFORE trim (expect mL31, endpoints [0,50,0]/[50,50,0]); trim({id, curveIds:[leftH]}) (expect VOID/mL31); positions(leftH) AFTER trim but BEFORE postTrim (KEY: mL51 dead-now vs mL31 still-alive); re-fetch containers -> SplittedCurves/NoneSplitted childCount deltas; nodeById(tree, leftH) -> parent container name if still present; then postTrim (expect mL31); getGeometry -> surviving h is the [50,100]->? right half only.
scripts.expected: trim VOID/mL31 (cite preTrim.md L79). KEY unknown: leftH_maxLevel_afterTrim records 31 (deferred) vs 51 (immediate death). Container deltas reveal whether trimmed seg is removed from SplittedCurves synchronously, moved to NoneSplitted (+1), or unchanged until postTrim. postTrim clean mL31. Survivor h endpoints measured via positions.
scripts.measurement: leftH_maxLevel_afterTrim (literal 31 or 51); splittedChildDelta and noneSplittedChildDelta (integers); leftH_parentAfterTrim (container name or null); survivor h endpoints via vecApprox; postTrimMaxLevel.

scripts.title: bulk trim: multi-segment, order-independence, untrimmed-id stability, trim-all-of-one-source
scripts.question: Can trim remove 3/5 segments atomically in one call? Is curveIds order-independent? Does trimming seg A churn untrimmed seg B's id? Does trimming ALL segments of one source remove that source while crossing cutters survive?
scripts.setup: makeSketch. Long horizontal lng=[0,50]->[200,50] crossed by 4 verticals at x=40,80,120,160 -> lng splits into 5 segments S0..S4 (left->right). preTrim; map the 5 lng segs by midpoint x via positions(); record ids in spatial order. (Verticals split into 2 each; ignored for lng probes.) Use addSketch for the order-independence twin fixture and the trim-all-of-source fixture (same part, NO 2nd part.create).
scripts.call: (a) Order: trim S1,S3 passing curveIds:[S3,S1] reversed -> VOID/mL31. (b) Stability: BEFORE that trim record S0,S2,S4 ids; AFTER trim before postTrim re-positions(S0,S2,S4) -> mL31 alive AND ids unchanged. (c) postTrim -> getGeometry survivors S0,S2,S4 are 3 disjoint lines (non-contiguous, do NOT coalesce; contrast preTrim.md L83). (d) Twin via addSketch: identical cross, trim [S1,S3] forward order -> compare survivor endpoints to (c) via vecApprox. (e) trim-all-of-source via addSketch: rebuild, trim ALL 5 lng segs [S0..S4] in ONE call -> VOID/mL31; postTrim -> lng fully gone from getGeometry.lines, only the 4 verticals' survivors remain; verify a crossing vertical's survivor endpoints intact.
scripts.expected: Multi-seg trim atomic VOID/mL31. Reversed vs forward order yield identical survivor geometry (set op). Untrimmed sibling ids STABLE and alive before postTrim. 3 disjoint survivors do not coalesce. trim-all-of-one-source removes lng entirely; crossing verticals survive (their segments may get new ids per preTrim.md L80).
scripts.measurement: multiTrim2Void; orderReversedSameResult (vecApprox survivor endpoints across twin fixtures); untrimmedSegsIdStable (id equality before/after) and untrimmedSegsAlive (mL31); survivorsAreThreeDisjoint (count=3, endpoints); trimAllFiveVoid; lngFullyRemoved (getGeometry.lines lacks any lng-spanning line); crossing vertical survivor endpoints vecApprox.

scripts.title: BOUNDED HANG PROBE: does trim inherit the trimCurves many-segment hang? (<=30 segs, run LAST)
scripts.question: Does trim slow super-linearly or hang as staged segment count rises on a lightly-constrained grid? Find the trimMs-vs-N trend across rungs ~12/~24/<=30 WITHOUT reproducing the proven 39-seg kill-9.
scripts.setup: RISK-FLAGGED. Header comment: '// WARNING HANG-RISK PROBE: bounded <=30 segs, lightly-constrained, ZERO manual dimensions. trimCurves hung at 39 segs / 20 constraints+20 dims (TODO build-lever-bracket). Run LAST; be ready to kill -9.' makeSketch (planeId so solver lives, but add NO manual dimensions/constraints -> auto-constraints only = lightly constrained, isolating segment-count from constraint-density). Three SEPARATE sketches via addSketch, built and finalized smallest-first: Tier1 grid ~12 segs (2 horizontals x 2 verticals full cross), Tier2 ~24 segs (3x3), Tier3 <=30 segs (3x3 alt or 4x2 — HARD CEILING 30, NEVER build toward 39/66). Total staged = Mh*(Mv+1)+Mv*(Mh+1); MEASURE actual N from preResult, do not trust arithmetic (collinear/corner-incidence may shift it).
scripts.call: Per tier (serial, fresh sketch, smallest first): preTrim({id}); N = preResult.result.flatMap(e=>e.splittedCurves.map(s=>s.id)).length; filewrite {tier,N} BEFORE trimming (so a hang loses no setup). Pick a moderate subset (~N/3, every other seg) -> t0=Date.now(); trim({id, curveIds:subset}) (each call guarded by the runner wall-clock cap; treat no-return-within-cap as a POSITIVE hang result, record N, do NOT retry, main agent restarts worker); trimMs=Date.now()-t0; record trim maxLevel/VOID; postTrim, record postTrimMs. Abort before next tier if trimMs climbs steeply.
scripts.expected: OPEN question. Outcomes: (A) all rungs return fast with flat trimMs -> trim does NOT inherit the hang at low constraint density (hang was constraint-density-driven). (B) trimMs grows super-linearly toward 30 -> segment-count-driven, trim inherits; extrapolate peg-N, document safe ceiling. (C) a rung times out / pegs CPU -> trim inherits the hang; record exact N, stop, main agent kill -9. Bounded <=30 ids, never 39.
scripts.measurement: Per-tier table {tier, N, trimSubsetCount, trimMs, postTrimMs, trimMax, postTrimMax}; trimMs_trend (3 numbers; flag super-linear if Tier3 >> 3x Tier1); allTiersVoid; noHangUpTo30Segs (boolean verdict); explicit verdict line answering 'does trim inherit the trimCurves hang and at what N'.

scripts.title: trim arg-shape validation: empty [], missing curveIds, missing id, duplicate [s,s]
scripts.question: Is curveIds:[] a safe mL31 no-op (NOT a trim-all footgun)? Missing curveIds -> 1004 or no-op? Missing id -> 1004? Is duplicate [s,s] idempotent or a double-free error?
scripts.setup: makeSketch. Canonical cross h+v -> preTrim -> 4 segs; capture all 4 ids; pick one seg s and record the OTHER 3 endpoints to prove non-destruction. Each sub-probe is its own guarded call capturing {maxLevel, codes, messages, result}; after each, getGeometry to confirm all 4 staged segs still alive (atomicity / no-op proof).
scripts.call: (a) trim({id, curveIds:[]}) (expect mL31 no-op, NOTHING removed — distinct from preTrim []=all). (b) trim({id}) missing curveIds (expect 1004 OR mL31 no-op — record which). (c) trim({curveIds:[s]}) missing id (expect mL51/1004, mirrors preTrim L108). (d) trim({id, curveIds:[s,s]}) duplicate (expect mL31, s trimmed once, idempotent — contrast preTrim L68 where dup ids split twice; then getGeometry confirms the OTHER 3 segs alive, s gone after postTrim).
scripts.expected: [] is a safe mL31 no-op (confirm NOT trim-all): follow-up getGeometry shows all 4 segs alive. missing curveIds: record 1004 vs no-op. missing id: 1004. duplicate [s,s]: VOID/mL31, idempotent single removal, other segs untouched.
scripts.measurement: emptyMaxLevel and emptyAllSegsAlive (count=4); missingCurveIdsMaxLevel+code; missingIdCode (expect 1004); dupMaxLevel (expect 31) + dupOtherSegsAlive (3 segs via positions) + dupTrimmedOnce (s gone after postTrim).

scripts.title: trim id-type rejection map: wrong-type id and wrong-type curveIds element (1001 list)
scripts.question: What error/code fires for a wrong-type id (part/point) vs a wrong-type curveIds element (sketch id, point id, constraint id)? What is trim's curveIds type-list in the 1001 message — ['sketch-curve'] like preTrim or narrower?
scripts.setup: makeSketch -> capture partId. Canonical cross h+v -> preTrim -> capture a valid seg. Also capture: the sketch's own id (skId), a sketch point id (via getPoints on a seg -> an endpoint id), and an Auto_* constraint id (from tree). Each probe its own guarded call; capture verbatim message text + code + the expected-type list string.
scripts.call: (a) trim({id: partId, curveIds:[validSeg]}) -> expect mL51/1001 ['sketch'] (inherited preTrim L110). (b) trim({id: pointId, curveIds:[validSeg]}) -> mL51/1001 ['sketch']. (c) trim({id: skId, curveIds:[skId]}) sketch's own id as curveId -> mL51/1001 ['sketch-curve']? OR 1006? OR no-op — THE open type-list question. (d) trim({id: skId, curveIds:[pointId]}) -> 1001 wrong type (is the list ['sketch-curve'] or narrower staged-segment?). (e) trim({id: skId, curveIds:[constraintId]}) -> 1001/1006.
scripts.expected: wrong-type id -> 1001 ['sketch']. curveIds element of wrong type -> the load-bearing unknown: 1001 with expected-list string (['sketch-curve'] vs narrower) vs 1006. Capture the verbatim ['...'] token from the 1001 message as the proof.
scripts.measurement: wrongTypeId_code (expect 1001) + wrongTypeId_list verbatim (expect ['sketch']); curveIdsSketchId_code+list; curveIdsPointId_code+list; curveIdsConstraintId_code; the exact expected-type string in each 1001 message.

scripts.title: trim atomicity & stale ids: dead-from-re-preTrim, mixed valid+bad, valid+source, re-trim already-trimmed
scripts.question: Is a stale/dead seg id (killed by re-preTrim or post-commit) rejected as 1006 or silently no-op? In a mixed batch, does one bad id atomic-fail leaving the valid seg MEASURABLY untouched? Does valid+sourceId poison the call or trim valid while ignoring source? Does re-trimming an already-trimmed seg mL31 no-op or 1006?
scripts.setup: makeSketch + several addSketch fixtures (one part). Fixture A: cross h+v -> preTrim -> capture segX -> preTrim AGAIN (segX now dead per preTrim.md L98). Fixture B (addSketch): cross -> preTrim -> capture validSeg + sourceId(h's original id) + a fresh seg s. Each probe captures exact code AND proves the intended survivor via positions endpoints (SOUL.md numeric atomicity proof).
scripts.call: (a) Stale-dead: trim({id, curveIds:[segX]}) on Fixture A after re-preTrim -> 1006 (dead=nonexistent) vs mL31 no-op (not-currently-staged) — record exact code. (b) Mixed valid+bogus: trim({id, curveIds:[validSeg, 999999]}) -> expect atomic mL51/1006; then positions(validSeg) AFTER -> original endpoints (cite preTrim.md L90 but CONFIRM survivor measured). (c) Mixed valid+sourceId: trim({id, curveIds:[validSeg, sourceId]}) -> record maxLevel: does the #155 silent-no-op element poison (mL51) or is validSeg trimmed while source ignored (mL31, validSeg dead)? (d) Re-trim: trim([s]) then trim([s]) again before postTrim -> 2nd call mL31 no-op vs 1006 (triangulates the dead-id rule with (a)).
scripts.expected: Stale-dead: open — 1006 vs mL31 (cite preTrim.md L98 as kill mechanism). Mixed valid+bogus: atomic fail mL51/1006, validSeg survives with measured original endpoints. Mixed valid+source: reveals whether silent-no-op tier is per-element or call-poisoning. Re-trim: open — no-op vs 1006; pairs with (a) to define the dead-vs-absent rule.
scripts.measurement: staleDead_code (31 or 51/1006); mixedBogus_maxLevel (51) + validSegSurvivesEndpoints (vecApprox original); mixedSource_maxLevel + validSegDied (boolean via positions); reTrim2nd_code (31 or 1006).

scripts.title: trim curveIds scoping: a seg id from ANOTHER sketch — 1006 not-in-this-sketch vs 1001 wrong-type vs global leniency
scripts.question: Does trim scope curveIds to THIS sketch's staging? A seg id from sk2 passed to trim on sk1 — atomic-fail 1006 (not in sk1), 1001 wrong-type, or does it leniently trim sk2's segment (inheriting splitCurve footgun #154 global geomId resolution)?
scripts.setup: makeSketch -> sk1 (cross h1+v1). addSketch -> sk2 (cross h2+v2). preTrim both (sequence carefully: preTrim sk1, capture a sk1 seg as survivor witness; preTrim sk2, capture seg_from_sk2). NOTE preTrim-twice-without-postTrim on the SAME sketch kills ids (preTrim.md L98) — here the two preTrims are on DIFFERENT sketches so both stagings should coexist; verify both seg sets alive before the cross probe.
scripts.call: trim({id: sk1, curveIds:[seg_from_sk2]}) -> record exact code. Then: positions(seg_from_sk2) to check whether it was leniently trimmed (mL51 after = trimmed in sk2 = global leniency like #154) or untouched; and positions of a sk1 witness seg to confirm sk1 staging untouched. Contrast with TODO #154 (splitCurve resolves geomId globally).
scripts.expected: Open: 1006 (trim scopes to sk1's staging, seg not found -> atomic fail) is the safe outcome; OR 1001 wrong-type; OR (footgun) silent mL31 + seg_from_sk2 actually trimmed in sk2 = trim inherits splitCurve's global-resolution leniency #154. This separates 'this-sketch staging membership check' from 'global existence check'.
scripts.measurement: crossSketch_code (1006 vs 1001 vs 31); crossSketch_segTrimmedInSk2 (boolean: positions(seg_from_sk2) mL51 after?); sk1WitnessUntouched (mL31, endpoints intact).

scripts.title: trim a CIRCLE arc segment vs a line segment; survivor arc correctness
scripts.question: Does trim accept a circle arc segment (from a doubly-cut circle) the same as a line segment (VOID/mL31)? Does the survivor arc get a NEW id with correct endpoints, and does an arc seg die immediately like a line seg?
scripts.setup: makeSketch. Circle C center (50,50) r 40 + line L=[0,50]->[100,50] through center -> L cuts C at (10,50) and (90,50); preTrim -> circle becomes 2 arcs (N not N+1, preTrim.md L41), line becomes 3 segs. From the circle entry identify the 2 arc seg ids; positions() each -> mL31 with endpoints near (10,50)/(90,50) (arc segs accept getPositions, unlike whole-circle parts preTrim.md L42/L46); classify top arc (midpoint y>50, e.g. (50,90)) vs bottom arc. Line-only control via addSketch.
scripts.call: trim({id, curveIds:[bottomArcId]}) -> assert VOID/mL31 (FIRST proof trim accepts an arc seg). positions(bottomArcId) AFTER trim before postTrim (immediate-death question for an arc, mirror script 01). postTrim. getGeometry -> arcs array with one survivor (top arc); positions survivor -> endpoints (10,50)/(90,50), midpoint side y>50; survivor id != bottomArcId and != original circle id (new id, preTrim.md L80). Control (addSketch): line-only cross, trim a line seg -> identical VOID/mL31 shape.
scripts.expected: Arc seg trims identically to a line seg (VOID/mL31). Survivor top arc has correct endpoints and a NEW id. Arc seg immediate-death matches the line-seg behavior measured in script 01. Line control confirms arc-vs-line parity.
scripts.measurement: arcSegsGetPositionsOk (both arcs mL31 with endpoints); trimArcVoid (VOID/mL31); bottomArc_maxLevel_afterTrim; survivorArcEndpoints vecApprox (10,50)/(90,50) + midpoint y>50; survivorArcNewId (!= bottom, != circle); lineSegTrimParity (control VOID/mL31).

scripts.title: round-trip endgame: trim-ALL->postTrim (empty sketch vs error), partial trim still postTrims clean, mixed trimmed+untrimmed-staged
scripts.question: If you trim EVERY staged seg then postTrim, do you get an empty sketch (geometry arrays length 0) or an error? Do leftover points / leaked NoneSplitted0 remain? Does a partial trim still postTrim cleanly, and does a mix of trimmed + untrimmed-staged finalize cleanly with correct id churn?
scripts.setup: makeSketch + addSketch fixtures (one part). A: cross h+v (4 segs); collect ALL 4. B (addSketch): cross, plan to trim only the 2 overhang segs (canonical L). C (addSketch): cross, plan to trim ONE overhang seg only (leave 3 staged untrimmed).
scripts.call: A trim-all: trim({id, curveIds:[all 4]}) (record VOID/maxLevel); postTrim (KEY: record maxLevel + messages); getGeometry -> record lines/arcs/circles/points array lengths (empty [] vs leftover points vs error); containers(tree) for leaked NoneSplitted0 (preTrim.md L100); then a second postTrim/preTrim on the empty sketch -> clean no-op? B partial: trim the 2 overhang segs; postTrim -> mL31, getGeometry shows clean L (2 lines meeting at (50,50)); confirm Auto_Coinc (CC_2DCoincidentConstraint) present at cut vertex (cite preTrim.md L85, light confirm). C mixed: trim ONE overhang seg only; postTrim -> mL31; untrimmed-staged segs restore to ORIGINAL ids (preTrim.md L80), the trimmed seg's survivor gets a NEW id.
scripts.expected: Trim-all->postTrim: open — empty sketch (all geometry arrays length 0) mL31 vs postTrim error mL51; document leftover points and NoneSplitted0 leak; empty-sketch re-postTrim clean no-op. Partial: clean L, Auto_Coinc present. Mixed: clean finalize, untrimmed keep original ids, trimmed survivor gets new id.
scripts.measurement: trimAllVoid + trimAll_postTrimMaxLevel + trimAll_postTrimMessages; sketchEmpty (lines/arcs/circles/points lengths, ideally all 0) + leftoverPoints count; noneSplittedLeak (NoneSplitted0 present?); emptyRePostTrimNoOp (mL31); partial_postTrimClean + autoCoincPresent (named constraint) + L endpoints vecApprox; mixed_postTrimClean + untrimmedRestoredOriginalIds (id equality) + trimmedSurvivorNewId.

scripts.title: minimal solver-independence: trim a line seg AND an arc seg on a planeless sketch
scripts.question: Does trim work on a planeless (solver-dead) sketch for both a line segment and an arc segment, confirming inherited solver-independence (no constraint solver needed)?
scripts.setup: makeSketch (creates the part), then addPlanelessSketch(api, partId, 'pl') — no planeId, dead constraint solver. On pl build a cross h+v AND a circle C center (50,50) r 40 cut by a line through center. Keep it minimal — single data point per the lens instruction, not a matrix.
scripts.call: preTrim({id: pl}) -> expect ok (<=mL31); trim({id: pl, curveIds:[oneLineSeg, oneArcSeg]}) (one line seg + one arc seg in one call) -> expect VOID/mL31, NO solver error; postTrim({id: pl}) -> mL31; getGeometry -> survivors correct via positions/vecApprox.
scripts.expected: All three calls <= mL31 with no solver-dependence error (inherited from preTrim solver-independence, preTrim.md). trim itself is NOT solver-dependent for either a line or an arc segment. One concise confirmation, not exhaustive.
scripts.measurement: planelessPreTrimMaxLevel; planelessTrimVoid (line+arc one call, VOID/mL31); planelessPostTrimMaxLevel; planelessSurvivorsCorrect (vecApprox endpoints of one line survivor + one arc survivor).

VALIDATION empty curveIds:[] is safe no-op NOT trim-all (script 04)
VALIDATION missing curveIds, missing id (1004), duplicate [s,s] idempotent (script 04)
ERROR-MAP id-type 1001 ['sketch'] and curveIds-element-type 1001 ['sketch-curve'] vs narrower (script 05)

STALE/dead seg id from re-preTrim and re-trim-already-trimmed -> 1006 vs mL31 no-op (script 06)

PROVEN facts cited to preTrim.md, NOT re-scripted: VOID/mL31, atomic 1006 baseline, #155 source no-op, multiple trim()/postTrim, nothing-staged no-op, consumes only splittedCurves[].id, trim([]) restores
openRisks: HANG (script 03): trim may peg the single shared worker at 99% CPU requiring kill -9, like trimCurves did at 39 segs. Mitigation: hard cap <=30 segs, lightly-constrained (zero manual dims), smallest-tier-first, per-call wall-clock guard, filewrite N before each trim so a hang loses no data, run LAST. A timeout is recorded as a POSITIVE hang finding — do NOT retry; main agent restarts the worker.

Scripts 01-02-08-09 build multi-crossing grids — if a fixture accidentally yields more segments than intended (corner incidence), a multi-seg trim could approach the hang zone. Mitigation: all non-03 fixtures kept to <=12 segments and <=5-id trims; MEASURE actual N from preResult before trimming; if N unexpectedly high, reduce before the trim call.

preTrim-twice-without-postTrim kills the first batch's seg ids (preTrim.md L98). Script 06 (stale-dead) relies on this; script 07 (cross-sketch) must preTrim on DIFFERENT sketches to keep both stagings alive — verify both seg sets alive before the cross probe or the test is invalid.

part.create works only ONCE per run (poisons drawing on 2nd call) — every script must call makeSketch exactly once and use addSketch/addPlanelessSketch for all additional sketches. A stray 2nd part.create silently nulls and invalidates the whole script.

getGeometry mid-workflow shows only ORIGINAL ids (preTrim.md L58) — staged seg ids and container state must be read from the response .structure.tree via containers()/nodeById, not from getGeometry.result. Scripts 01/09 depend on reaching the tree; if a call's response lacks .structure, fetch getGeometry({id}).structure.tree explicitly.

Whole-circle parts reject getPositions (preTrim.md L42); script 08 must confirm the targeted ids are ARC segments (2-point cut) not whole-circle parts before asserting endpoints, else use centerPos fallback.

trim's curveIds type-list (script 05 B-probes) and the stale/cross-sketch codes (06a, 07) are genuinely unknown — expected values are hypotheses; the script must record literal codes/messages and not assert a presumed code, per SOUL.md numeric-proof discipline.

Atomicity claims (script 06b/06d) require a MEASURED survivor coordinate (getPositions endpoints) after the failed call, not merely 'the call errored' — a passing maxLevel assertion alone does not prove valid segs untouched.
